Pressure canning is intimidating the first couple of times it's done. However, it's worth it and like anything else, once you learn it's easy.

Tomatoes are good- don't get slicing tomatoes though. You'll want to can Romas. I enjoy keeping an entire shelf of quarts of tomatoes for the reasons you listed. You'll need to skin them first. Just toss them in boiling water until the skin cracks and then throw them in a sink filled with cold water. The peels will slip right off and you toss them directly into a sanitized jar and add a little salt and a little lemon juice- boom you're golden. Press everything down to make sure there are no air pockets and of course wipe down the lip of the jar before adding the lids. The tomatoes and juice look weird after they've been canned because they separate. Don't worry about it- after 24 hours you can shake them and they'll look pretty again.

As for a jelly, just pick whatever is in season and is cheap. Don't plan on doing both projects on the same day and remember that jellies must be made in small batches (otherwise they won't gel).
